decision: the native engine cannot interleave at all: its serve loop is one request per iteration (GEN/GENI only, generate.cpp:3395) and --batch/--slots are parsed only by src/qwen35/q36_engine.cu:4354; prod's /cfg/lamina.json has no parallel, so the server's slot protocol (engine_batch.cpp: BGEN/BADM/BYIELD) is dead code for Flash-Next and a second request waits for the first's DONE
why: the received framing assumed a FIFO lock plus a reader that exists; on this engine the reader does not exist, so the running decode is undisturbed and the whole cost is queueing
evidence: generate.cpp:3395, q36_engine.cu:4354, config.cpp:325 (parallel->--batch), docker inspect lamina (no batch in args)

decision: TTFT decomposes into decode-turn queue + reads ahead + own read; measured on the shipping binary: B (29,022-token cold prompt, arriving 10 s into a 25 s generation) TTFT 22.6 s = 16.8 queue + 5.8 own read; C (278 tokens) 21.6 s = 14.8 queue + 6.8 a read ahead + 0.1 own; A's rate untouched (171 tok/s avg, 178-190 per 2 s bucket while two queued); the same 29K prompt warm costs 0.14 s
why: read-beside-decode removes only the two read terms (a 26-30% TTFT cut measured), because keeping decode single-stream is its own simplification; the majority term is the exclusive decode turn, and on this box's warm traffic the read terms are already near zero

decision: the next gate is P1 conversation resume fidelity/cost (option A, server-side preemption: STOP, park, run the queued request, re-issue with the produced ids), the only design that touches the dominant term with no engine work; decode batching stays the only fix that removes it for everyone, and it is parked for expert-working-set reasons not scheduling ones
why: measured attribution beats the received framing's 3-10x claim; the cheap thing to test is the thing that attacks 15-17 s of 22.6 s, not the 6 s term
evidence: plans/batching-reconsidered.md (why batching is parked); plans/03-read-beside-decode/overview.md gate 2

decision: the preemption card is real and cheap at the id level: a parked conversation restores in 0.16 s at 5,596 tokens (0.55 s at 5,096, 0.93 s via the API at ~6K) against 1.15-1.57 s to cold-read a smaller prompt, so the parked K/V covers what decoding wrote; a chat-template continuation is NOT byte-safe (a 1,369-char cut made the model restart its own count, a 1,200-char cut continued identically) so re-issue must be GEN prompt+produced ids
why: identity of a resumed generation is the remaining gate, and the server already has the hard part: legs in engine_batch.cpp (#1869 carry, may_go_solo) resume a request across STOP and re-issue, so preemption is a policy on existing machinery
result: cost and mechanism answered, identity open

decision: P1c OOM'd the host: wrapper resumed at 12:47:56, a request summoned prod at 12:48:03, the e2e engine loaded its 56 GiB pinned arena ~1 min later; pause does not wait for the 120s docker stop or the arena back, so two arenas (85 GiB anon, 113 MiB free, swap untouched) rebooted the box
why: run-e2e.sh's pause-only guard was the flaw and I did not verify prod was down and its memory returned before loading a second engine; earlier runs passed on luck, not on the guard
evidence: journalctl -b -1 12:48-12:56 (page allocation failure -> OOM report); run-e2e.sh --probe now reports prod running + 23941 MiB free and would refuse
result: hardened: preflight waits for prod gone + 64 GiB free, 3s watchdog docker-kills on prod return or <20 GiB, container capped at 72g

decision: identity CLOSED against policy-only preemption: the park's restore is byte-exact (same prompt twice: 362/362 tokens identical from a checkpoint re-read; a run stopped at the cut matches the control for 181 and 271 tokens), but re-issuing ids diverges within 0-10 tokens because the protocol must re-feed the last PRODUCED token, and the prompt/verify path writes different K/V bytes for a token than the decode path does; the +1 trick proved the saved state itself is exact (4278 ids, 4276 cached in 77 ms, ~1.1 GB/s at ~4.3K cells)
why: the internal contrast is the proof: re-feeding a token the control wrote via the PROMPT path is byte-exact (G and C0), re-feeding ONE token the control wrote via DECODE is not (C1) - so exactness needs reuse==n in reusable() plus a serve loop that decodes with nothing to feed, not the batching port
evidence: ~/strata-data/bench/2026-11-12/p1d-det.log p1d-det-engine.log; plans/03-read-beside-decode/overview.md P1c and P1d; harness/ holds the drivers
result: P1c's 284/156 divergences were this same mechanism plus config drift; exact preemption is now one narrow engine change away, and the open call is whether to make it or accept drift

decision: retracted my own P1 headline: the parked K/V does NOT come back for a mid-generation re-issue, and the 0.16 s restore was a prompt-cache hit on the SECOND re-issue of the same ids (first: 4559 ids 4095 cached in 524 ms; second: 4558 cached in 146 ms) - the correct rule is that reuse can only land on a CHECKPOINT (prompt/turn boundaries, every --prompt-cache-every, and a park's end), and nothing checkpoints mid-generation
why: I read TTFT as the measurement when the engine log's cached-token count was the measurement; a cost number that does not name what was re-read is not a measurement
evidence: conversation_cache.hpp:77-100 reusable(), prompt_cache.cpp:136-186 stash_live(); both engine logs above
